prompt: What is the return type of `CourseRow`?
hint: It emits instead of returning.

choices.text: `Unit`
choices.why: Right: a composable that emits returns nothing; it adds nodes to the composition.

choices.text: `View`
choices.why: Compose emits nodes, not views; `View` is the old system.

choices.text: `Column`, the layout it creates
choices.why: `Column` is called, not returned; its node is emitted.

choices.text: A `Composable` object that Compose draws later
choices.why: There is no such object; the function's calls are the description.

prompt: `summary(course): String` calls `CourseRow` and the build fails. What is the right fix?
hint: Does `summary` draw anything?

choices.text: Mark `summary` as `@Composable`
choices.why: It would compile and make a function that computes a string callable only during composition.

choices.text: Take the `CourseRow` call out
choices.why: Right: a function that computes stays plain, and a composable calls it, never the other way round.

choices.text: Wrap the call in `setContent { }`
choices.why: `setContent` belongs to an activity, and `summary` is not one.

choices.text: Pass a `Composer` argument by hand
choices.why: The composer is added by the compiler plugin; it is not something you pass.

prompt: Why is `stringResource` named in camelCase while `CourseRow` is in PascalCase, although both are composables?
hint: One of them gives you something back.

choices.text: `stringResource` is not a composable
choices.why: It is: it reads the current configuration, which needs composition.

choices.text: PascalCase is for composables in Material only
choices.why: `CourseRow` is the planner's own and follows the same rule.

choices.text: It returns a value instead of emitting
choices.why: Right: emitters read as nouns, value-returners as ordinary functions.

choices.text: camelCase marks a composable that may be skipped
choices.why: Naming has no effect on skipping; it is a convention for readers.

prompt: The compiler plugin gives every composable a hidden extra parameter, the ___, through which it reaches the tree.
hint: A noun from the verb to compose.

prompt: What makes `CourseRow` stateless?
hint: Where does its data come from?

choices.text: Everything it shows arrives as a parameter
choices.why: Right: data in, a description out.

choices.text: It has no `@Composable` annotation
choices.why: It has it; stateless is about where data comes from.

choices.text: It is never recomposed
choices.why: It recomposes whenever its parameters change.

choices.text: It is declared in the `data` package with the model
choices.why: It is in `ui`; the package is not what makes it stateless.

prompt: In Compose's own components, which optional parameter comes first by convention?
hint: Lesson 6 is about it.

choices.text: `enabled: Boolean = true`
choices.why: It comes after the modifier in `Button`.

choices.text: `content`, the slot
choices.why: The slot goes last, so it can be written in braces.

choices.text: `modifier: Modifier = Modifier`
choices.why: Right: it lets the caller decide size, padding and position.

choices.text: `onClick`
choices.why: `onClick` is required, with no default, and comes before.

prompt: A teammate rewrites `CourseRow(courseId: String)` so that the row loads its own course from the database. What does the planner lose first?
hint: Section 04 is next.

choices.text: Nothing at all: the call site gets shorter and every screen looks the same
choices.why: The call is shorter, and every listed advantage is gone.

choices.text: Previewing or testing the row with no database behind it
choices.why: Right: a stateless row can be shown with any data; this one needs the real source.

choices.text: Recomposition, which only works with parameters
choices.why: A composable recomposes whatever it reads; the loss is elsewhere.

choices.text: Translation, since ids cannot be translated
choices.why: The name would still come from the course; translation is untouched.

prompt: Match each part of `Button`'s parameter list to why it sits where it does.
hint: Required, layout, the rest, content.

pairs.right: Required, so it comes first with no default
The caller's say over size and position
Last, so it can be written in braces after the call

prompt: Which command rendered the planner's previews to PNG files?
hint: It belongs to the Android CLI.

choices.text: `./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug`
choices.why: That records screenshots from tests, as lesson 2 did; previews went through the CLI.

choices.text: `android preview render`
choices.why: Right, with `--fqn` naming each preview and `-o` the output directory.

choices.text: `adb shell screencap`
choices.why: That needs a device, which the recording machine did not have.

choices.text: `./gradlew assembleDebug`
choices.why: It builds an APK and renders nothing.

prompt: Why does the lesson keep a second preview with `fontScale = 1.5f`?
hint: Who sets that on a phone?

choices.text: To test that the strings are translated
choices.why: Translation is a locale, not a font scale.

choices.text: Because a preview at 1.0 renders blurry
choices.why: The first preview rendered cleanly.

choices.text: It is what a phone does when its owner chooses larger text
choices.why: Right: many people use the setting, and the row must grow with it.

choices.text: Android Studio requires two previews per file
choices.why: There is no such requirement.

prompt: `file` measured the normal preview at 249 by 105 pixels. How many pixels wide was the one at `fontScale = 1.5f`?
hint: About one and a half times.

prompt: A preview of a screen comes out as an empty box, while the app shows the screen fine. Which cause fits section 04 best?
hint: What does a preview NOT start?

choices.text: It loads its own data, which nothing supplies there
choices.why: Right: a preview runs the composable only, with no activity, `ViewModel` or network.

choices.text: Previews ignore `MaterialTheme`
choices.why: The planner's previews used it and drew its typography.

choices.text: The preview has `showBackground = true`
choices.why: That only paints a background behind the content.

choices.text: The composable is in a file without any other preview functions
choices.why: One preview per file is enough to render.

prompt: In `PlannerCard(title, content)`, what does the line `content()` do?
hint: It is a call.

choices.text: Returns the caller's composables as a list
choices.why: Nothing is returned; the lambda emits.

choices.text: Runs the caller's lambda, which emits inside the card's column
choices.why: Right: the rows land after the title, inside the frame.

choices.text: Draws the card's background
choices.why: `Card` draws the background; `content()` adds the caller's part.

choices.text: Schedules the content for the next frame
choices.why: It runs now, during composition.

prompt: How many slots does `Scaffold` have, by the lesson's count?
hint: Bars, a host, a button and the content.

prompt: Should `CourseRow` take a slot for the course's name instead of a `Course`?
hint: Who should decide how the name is drawn?

choices.text: Yes: slots are always more flexible than data
choices.why: Flexibility here means every caller draws the name differently.

choices.text: Yes, because a slot recomposes less
choices.why: The choice is about who decides content, not about recomposition.

choices.text: No, until two real callers need different content there
choices.why: Right: pass data the component knows how to show; make a slot when callers truly differ.

choices.text: No, because slots cannot hold `Text`
choices.why: A slot can hold any composable, `Text` included.

prompt: `CourseRow` is called twice in `PlannerCardPreview`. How many `CourseRow` nodes are in the composition?
hint: The tree mirrors the calls.

choices.text: One, shared by both calls
choices.why: Each call is its own node with its own position.

choices.text: Two
choices.why: Right: one per call, each with its own parameters.

choices.text: None: only `Text` nodes are kept
choices.why: Every composable call is a node; only some of them draw.

prompt: Put the three things Compose does to show a frame in order.
hint: Section 06 names them.
items: composition: run the composables and record the tree
layout: measure and place each node
drawing: paint the nodes that draw

prompt: A value read by one `Text` deep in the tree changes. What does Compose run again?
hint: Not the whole tree.

choices.text: Everything from `setContent` down
choices.why: Compose does not rebuild from the top.

choices.text: The activity's `onCreate`
choices.why: Recomposition happens inside the composition, not in the activity.

choices.text: The composables that read the value, compared against the tree
choices.why: Right: that is recomposition, lesson 5's subject.

choices.text: Only the drawing step, since text is pixels
choices.why: A new value can change what is emitted, so composition runs for the readers.

prompt: After the test changed the minutes three times, how many entries did the `opened` list hold?
hint: The first composition counts too.

choices.why: That is what the line was meant to record, and not what it did.
The first composition ran the body too.
Right: one composition and three recompositions.
120 was the minutes on screen, which were right.

prompt: The planner must load a course's sessions once when its screen appears. Where does that work go?
hint: Compose runs one thing once and cancels it when the composable leaves.

choices.text: In the composable's body, before the first `Text`
choices.why: The body runs on every recomposition, so it would load again and again.

choices.text: In a `LaunchedEffect`
choices.why: Right, and lesson 11 uses it; lesson 10 moves the loading itself into a `ViewModel`.

choices.text: In the preview function
choices.why: A preview never runs in the app.

choices.text: In `onClick` of the first row
choices.why: That runs when somebody taps, not when the screen appears.

prompt: Which of these are safe in the body of a composable? Choose all that apply.
hint: Does running it ten times change anything outside the screen?

choices.text: Formatting the minutes as text from a parameter
choices.why: Yes: it depends only on the input and changes nothing.

choices.text: Appending to a list of screen views
choices.why: No: section 07's bug.

choices.text: Calling a composable for each course in a list parameter
choices.why: Yes: that is describing the screen.

choices.text: Saving the current course to a file
choices.why: No: it would write on every recomposition.

prompt: Why did the screen show the right total, 120, while the list was wrong?
hint: Which of the two lines describes?

choices.text: Describing again with new data is what recomposition is for; appending is not describing
choices.why: Right: the `Text` was replaced each time, the list only grew.

choices.text: The list is printed before the last recomposition
choices.why: `waitForIdle` let every recomposition finish first.

choices.text: `Text` is skipped, and `opened` is not
choices.why: `WeekTotal` ran four times, and `Text` with it.

choices.text: The test reads `minutes` from a different thread
choices.why: Threads are not the issue; the side effect is.

hint: The CLI needs a preview to find.

prompt: A composable shows a list of sessions and also sends an analytics event `sessions_viewed` in its body. Users scroll and add sessions. What do the analytics show?
hint: When does the body run?

choices.text: One event per visit, as intended
choices.why: The body runs on every recomposition, not once per visit.

choices.text: No events, since composables cannot call network code
choices.why: Nothing stops the call; that is the problem.

choices.text: Many more events than visits
choices.why: Right: every change it reads reruns the body and sends another.

choices.text: Exactly one event per session added
choices.why: Additions are one cause among several; nothing makes it exactly one.

prompt: Which change lets `PlannerCard` hold the week's summary, a course's sessions and a list of reminders without learning about any of them?
hint: It is already in its signature.

choices.text: A `content: @Composable () -> Unit` slot
choices.why: Right: the card owns the frame, the caller what goes in it.

choices.text: A `type` parameter with one branch per kind of card
choices.why: Then the card would have to learn about every kind.

choices.text: Three separate card composables
choices.why: That repeats the frame three times instead of sharing it.

choices.text: Making the title a slot too
choices.why: The title is data the card knows how to show.
